translations.text: Paul the apostle, not from men, nor through men, but through Jesus Christ and God the Father, who raised him from the dead,
and all the brothers who are with me, to the churches of Galatia:
grace to you and peace from God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ,
who gave himself for our sins, so that he might deliver us from this evil world by the will of God and our Father,
to whom be glory forever and ever. Amen.
I am amazed that you are so quickly turning away from him who called you by the grace of Christ, to another gospel,
which is not another; but there are some who stir you up and want to pervert the gospel of Christ.
But even if we, or an angel from heaven, should preach to you anything apart from what we preached to you, let him be accursed!
As I said before, and now say again: if anyone preaches to you anything apart from what you received, let him be accursed!
Am I now to trust men, or God? Or do I seek in any way to please men? For if I were still pleasing men, I would not be a servant of Christ.
But I make known to you, brothers, concerning the gospel that was preached to you by me, that it is not according to man.
For I did not receive it from a man, nor did I learn it, but through the revelation of Jesus Christ.
For you have heard of my former way of life in Judaism, that I persecuted the churches of God beyond measure and ravaged them.
And I advanced in Judaism beyond many of my contemporaries among my own people; I was exceedingly zealous for the teachings of my fathers.
But when it pleased God, who chose me from my mother's womb and called me by his grace,
to reveal his Son through me, so that I might preach him among the Gentiles, I did not immediately make it known to flesh and blood,
nor did I go up to Jerusalem to those who were apostles before me, but I went to Arabia and returned again to Damascus.
Then after three years I went up to Jerusalem to see Peter, and I stayed with him fifteen days.
But I saw no other of the apostles, except James, the brother of the Lord.
And what I am writing to you, behold, before the Lord, I am not lying.
Then I came to the regions of Syria and Cilicia.
But I was unknown by face to the churches of Judea that were in Christ;
they had only heard it said that he who once persecuted us now preaches the faith that he once ravaged.
And they glorified God because of me.
Then in the fourteenth year I went up again to Jerusalem with Barnabas; I took Titus along with me as well.
And I went up by revelation and made known to them the gospel that I preach among the Gentiles, but privately to those who were held in esteem, lest perhaps I should be running or had run in vain.
But not even Titus, who was with me, though he was a Gentile, was compelled to be circumcised.
Because of those false brothers who had come in, who came in to spy out our freedom, which I have through Christ Jesus, so that they might enslave us,
to whom we did not submit for even one moment, so that the truth of the gospel might remain with you.

But as for those who supposed that they were something, those who had once been [something], they are in no way better than I. God does not look at a person's face. For those who were held in esteem told me nothing more,
but on the contrary, they knew that the gospel of the uncircumcision had been entrusted to me, just as that of the circumcision had been to Peter.
For he who helped Peter as apostle of the circumcision also helped me toward the Gentiles.

And when they recognized the grace that had been given to me, James and Cephas and John, who considered themselves pillars, gave me and Barnabas the right hand of fellowship, that we should go to the Gentiles and they to the circumcision.
Only that we should remember the poor, which very thing we were also eager to do.
And when Peter came to Antioch, I opposed him to his face, because he was in the wrong.
For before certain people came from James, he ate with the Gentiles; but when they came, he withdrew and separated himself, because he was afraid of those of the circumcision.
And the other Jews also became double-hearted along with him, so that even Barnabas was carried along by their double-heartedness.

But when I saw that they were not walking straight toward the truth of the gospel, I said to Peter in front of everyone: If you are a Jew and live in the manner of the Gentiles and not of the Jews, how can you compel the Gentiles to live as Jews?
We are Jews by nature and not sinners from among the Gentiles;

and we know that a person is not justified by works of the law, but by faith in Jesus Christ, and we have believed in Jesus Christ, so that we may be justified by faith in Jesus Christ and not by works of the law; for by works of the law no flesh will be justified.
If by this we seek justification in Christ, we too have been found sinners; so then, has Christ become a servant of sin? May it not be!
For if I build up again the very thing I tore down, I count myself a transgressor of the law.
For through the law I died to the law, so that I might live to God. I have been crucified with Christ.
And it is no longer I who live, but Christ lives in me. And the life I now live in the flesh, I live by faith in the Son of God, who loved me and gave himself for me.
I do not despise the grace of God. For if righteousness comes from the law, then did Christ die in vain?
O foolish Galatians, who has envied you, so that you do not obey the truth, you before whose eyes Jesus Christ crucified was openly portrayed among you beforehand?
I want to learn only this from you: did you receive the Spirit by the works of the law, or by hearing with faith?
Are you so foolish? You began spiritually, and now you are finishing carnally?
Have you suffered so much in vain? If indeed it was in vain!
So then, he who gave you the Spirit and works mighty deeds among you, does he do it from works of the law or by the hearing of faith?
Just as Abraham believed God, and it was counted to him as righteousness.
Do you know, then, that those who are of faith are the children of Abraham?
For the Scripture knew beforehand that God justifies the Gentiles by faith, and it announced the good news beforehand to Abraham: "In you all the Gentiles shall be blessed."
So then, those who are of faith are blessed together with that believing Abraham. (6)
For as many as are of the works of the law are under a curse. For it is written: "Cursed be everyone who does not abide by all that is written in the book of this law, to do it."
And that no one is justified by the law before God is clear, for: "The righteous shall live by faith."
But the law is not of faith; rather, if any man does it, he shall live by it.
Christ redeemed us from the curse of the law and came under a curse for us. For it is written: "Cursed be everyone who hangs on a tree."
This was so that the blessing of Abraham might come to the Gentiles through Jesus Christ Jesus [?], so that we might receive the promise of the Spirit by faith.
Brothers, I speak in human terms: no one disregards a man's confirmed document, or issues another order on top of it.
Now these promises were spoken to Abraham and to his seed. It does not say to him, "and to seeds," as of many, but as of one: "and to your seed," which is Christ.

And this I say: the document of the promise, confirmed by God with regard to Christ, is not made unconfirmed by the law, which came four hundred and thirty years afterward, so as to do away with that promise.
For if the inheritance is from the law, it is no longer from the promise; but God granted it to Abraham by means of the promise.
What then is the law? It was given on account of transgression, until the seed to whom the promise was made should come, and was ordained through angels by the hand of a mediator?
Now a mediator is not of one, but God is one.
Is the law then an enemy of the promises of God? May it not be! For if a law had been given that was able to give life, then righteousness would truly have come from the law.
But the Scripture shut up everything under sin, so that the promise, from the faith of Jesus Christ, might be given to those who believe.
But before faith came, we were enclosed under the law and shut up until the revealing of that future faith.
Therefore the law became our tutor toward Christ, so that we might be justified by faith.
But now that faith has come, we are no longer under guardians.
For you are all children of God through faith in Christ Jesus.
For as many of you as were baptized into Christ have put on Christ.
There is no Jew nor Gentile; there is no slave nor free; there is no distinction of male nor female, for you are all one in Christ Jesus.
And if you are Christ's, then you are indeed children of Abraham and heirs from the promise.
And this I say: as long as the heir is a child, he is in no way better than a slave, although he is lord of everything.
Rather, he is under household managers and stewards until he comes to take the place of his father.
So it was with us too: while we were still children, we were weighed down under the rules of this world.
But when the end of the times came, God sent his Son, born of a woman, and he came under the law,
so that he might redeem those who were under the law, and so that we might receive adoption as sons.
And because you are sons, God has sent forth the Spirit of his Son into our hearts, by whom we cry out: Abba, Father.
From now on you are no longer a slave, but a son; and if a son, then also an heir of God through Christ.
But at that time you did not know God, and you served those who by nature were not gods.
But now you have come to know God, or rather, God has known you. How can you turn back again to that weak and poor order, to which you wish to be enslaved all over again?
You observe days and months, seasons and years.
I fear for you, that I may have laboured over you in vain.
Become as I am, for I was as you are, brothers, I beg you. You have done me no wrong.
And you know that it was through weakness of the flesh that I first preached the gospel to you;
and you did not scorn or loathe the trial in my flesh, but you received me as an angel of God, as Christ Jesus.
What then has become of that blessedness of yours? For I testify to you that, if it had been possible, you would have plucked out your eyes and given them to me.
Have I then become some kind of enemy to you, I who tell you the truth?
They are zealous for you, not for good, but they want your overturning, so that you may emulate them.
But it is good to be zealous for what is good always, and not only at that coming of mine to you.
My children, for whom I am again in labor pains until Christ is formed among you.
And I wish to come to you now and to change my voice, for I am astonished at you. 9
Tell me, you who want to be under the law, have you not read the law?
For it is written that Abraham had two sons: one from the slave woman and one from the free woman.
But the one from the slave woman was born according to the flesh, while the one of the free woman was from the promise.
This is an allegory, for these women are the two laws: the one from Mount Sinai, bearing children into slavery, which is Hagar.
For Hagar is Mount Sinai in Arabia, and she corresponds to this present Jerusalem, for she is in slavery together with her children.
But the heavenly Jerusalem is free, which is the mother of us all.

For it is written: Rejoice, you barren one who do not bear; lift up your voice and cry out, you who have had no labor pains, for many are the children of the desolate woman, more than of her who had a husband.
But we, brothers, are children of the promise through Isaac.
But just as at that time the one born according to the flesh persecuted the spiritual one, so it is also now.
But what does Scripture say? Drive out that slave woman and her son, for the son of the slave woman shall not inherit with the son of the free woman.
So we, brothers, are not children of the slave woman, but of the free woman.
In that freedom with which Christ has set us free, stand firm, and do not take upon yourselves again the yoke of slavery. 10
Behold, I, Paul, tell you that if you are circumcised, Christ will profit you nothing.
And again I testify to every circumcised man that he is obligated to keep the whole law.
You have been cut off from Christ, you who are justified by the law; you have fallen away from grace.
For we, by the Spirit, through faith, await the hope of righteousness.
For in Christ Jesus neither circumcision has any power, nor uncircumcision, but faith, helped by love.
You were running well; who has made you stumble, so that you do not obey the truth?
That obedience does not come from the one who called you.
A little leaven leavens the whole batch of dough.
I trust in you through the Lord that you will think nothing else; but the one who is stirring you up will bear the judgment, whoever he may be.
But as for me, brothers, if I am preaching circumcision, why then am I persecuted? Has that stumbling block of the cross been done away with?
It would be fitting that those who are troubling you were removed far from you.
For you have been called to freedom, brothers; only do not let that freedom be a pretext for the flesh, but through love serve one another.
For the whole law is fulfilled in one word: You shall love your neighbor as yourself.
But if you bite and devour one another, see that you are not consumed by one another.
And this I say to you: let us walk by the Spirit, and do not fulfill the desire of the flesh.
For the flesh desires against the Spirit, and the Spirit against the flesh; and these are opposed to one another, so that you do not do what you want.
If you live by the Spirit, you are not under the law.
For the works of the flesh are plain, which are: acts of fornication, adulteries, impurities, filthy acts,
idolatries, sorceries, enmities, quarrels, jealousies, fits of anger, heresies, dissensions,

envies [?], murders, debaucheries, drunkenness, carousings, and things like these. Of these I tell you beforehand, as I told you before, that those who do such things will not inherit the kingdom of God.
But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faith,
Quietness, fasting, patience. Against such things there is no law.
And those who are Christ's have crucified their flesh with its passions and desires.
If we live by the Spirit, let us also stand by the Spirit.
Let us not be arrogant, accusing one another or envying one another.
Brothers, if someone is caught in some fault, you who are spiritual should set such a person right in a spirit of peace. Watch yourself, so that you are not tempted as well.
Bear one another's burden, and in this way fulfill the law of Christ.
For if anyone thinks that he is something when he is nothing, he deceives himself.
But let each person test his own works, and then he will have boasting in himself alone and not in relation to his neighbor,
for each person will bear his own burden.
And let the ignorant one share in the word of the teacher in every good thing.
Do not be deceived; God is not treated with contempt. For whatever a person sows, that he will also reap.
For whoever sows in his own flesh will reap corruption from his own flesh; but whoever sows to his own spirit will reap eternal life from his own spirit.
And let us not grow weary of doing good, for in its own time we will reap, if we do not lose heart.
Now therefore, while we still have time, let us do good to all, and especially to those of the household of faith.
Now see how many letters I have written to you with my own hand.
Those who want to make a fair appearance in the flesh are the ones who compel you to be circumcised, only so that they may not follow the cross of Christ.
For not even those who are circumcised keep the law themselves, but they want you to be circumcised, so that they may boast in that flesh of yours.
But far be it from me to boast, except in the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ, through which the world has been crucified to me, and I to the world.
For through Christ Jesus neither circumcision has any power, nor uncircumcision, but a new creation.
And as many as abide by this rule, peace be upon them and mercy, and upon the Israel of God.
From now on let no one cause me trouble; for I bear the brand-marks of the Lord Jesus in my body.
The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit, brothers. Amen.
